claims.text: Toughness retention in FCC high-entropy alloys is governed by synergy between heterogeneous lattice-strain-induced dislocation mechanisms and deformation twinning.
Multicomponent elemental mixing creates local variations in stacking-fault energy.
Local variations in stacking-fault energy promote deformation nano-twinning.
Heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors, including multiple kinks or jogs and bidirectional cross-slip.
Nano-twinning and unusual dislocation behavior jointly mitigate stress concentrations and delay crack propagation.
A near-equimolar CrCoNi-type alloy can provide a single-phase FCC baseline exhibiting mobile dislocations and significant nano-twinning.
Reducing or substituting an element that strongly lowers local stacking-fault energy will reduce the heterogeneity of the stacking-fault-energy landscape.
Local lattice-strain heterogeneity produces a distribution of stacking-fault energies.
The stacking-fault-energy distribution controls the density and spatial distribution of deformation twins.
Regions of lower stacking-fault energy facilitate dislocation cross-slip.
Deformation twins provide an additional plastic-deformation mode that supports toughness.
Dislocation cross-slip reduces stress intensity at crack tips.
Reducing stacking-fault-energy heterogeneity will suppress deformation-twin formation.
Reducing stacking-fault-energy heterogeneity will produce more localized dislocation pile-ups.
Reduced twin density and increased dislocation pile-up will decrease fracture toughness relative to the baseline.
Alloys retaining a heterogeneous stacking-fault-energy profile will retain superior toughness under identical loading.
A baseline combining robust dislocation mobility and abundant nano-twinning exhibits high strength-ductility synergy and retained toughness.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase FCC high-entropy alloys and similar near-equimolar systems.
The mechanism may not apply to multiphase, predominantly BCC, or predominantly HCP alloys because their governing deformation mechanisms differ.
Between room and cryogenic temperatures, CrCoNi simultaneously exhibits enhanced strength, ductility, and toughness, with nano-twinning contributing an important additional deformation mode.
